STEP 1 - Scene: A small portion of cooked meat (looks like sliced steak or roast pork/beef with a herb/garlic crust and a few green herb bits) on a white square plate, photographed from above, near-overhead angle. Only a few pieces remain.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White square plate, roughly 26 cm across (side). Area ≈ 26 x 26 ≈ 676 cm^2 (using the square's full width; a round-equivalent of 26 cm diameter gives 530 cm^2, so I use ~600 cm^2 as a compromise for the rounded-square shape).

STEP 3 - Items: (a) cooked meat pieces, pinkish-centered, with a brown seasoned crust; (b) small green herb bits and a little orange/red garnish fleck; (c) a few crumbs of crust.

STEP 4 - Area: Meat pieces together cover roughly 20% of the plate (about 120 cm^2). Herb and garnish bits about 1% (about 6 cm^2). Total food coverage ≈ 21%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Meat pile ~120 cm^2 x 1.5 cm ≈ 180 ml. Herb/garnish ~6 cm^2 x 0.5 cm ≈ 3 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Meat 180 ml x 0.95 ≈ 170 g. Herbs 3 ml x 0.15 ≈ 0.5 g, round to 1 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked beef/pork roast-type meat ≈ 200 kcal/100 g (fattier cuts with crust). Meat 170 g x 2.0 = 340 kcal. Herbs ~ 1 g x 30 kcal/100 g ≈ 0.3 kcal, negligible.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The visible remnants are roughly 4–5 bite-sized pieces, and 170 g of meat is plausibly a generous portion, though these pieces look somewhat smaller. A more conservative figure is about 120–150 g. I'll keep the estimate at the lower end of the calculation: about 140 g, which gives roughly 280 kcal. Total visible food ≈ 140 g, ≈ 280 kcal.
